body.question: What if I moved to Germany while keeping my current remote job?

proposal.interpretation: You are considering moving to Germany while continuing to work remotely for your current employer. I assumed the move is permanent and that you will keep the same job duties and salary.

branches.name: Full relocation
branches.description: Move to Germany and work entirely remotely from there.

branches.name: Split residency
branches.description: Spend part of the year in Germany and part in your current country, maintaining dual residency.

branches.name: Stay home
branches.description: Keep your current location and do not move to Germany.

variables.label: Visa or residence status
variables.why: Determines legal ability to stay and work in Germany.

variables.label: Employer permits remote work from abroad
variables.why: Your job must be allowed to be performed outside the home country.

variables.label: Will you become a German tax resident
variables.why: Tax residency affects how income is taxed.

variables.label: Cost of living level
variables.why: Higher or lower living costs change disposable income.

variables.label: German language proficiency
variables.why: Language skill influences daily life and integration.

questions: Will your employer formally approve remote work from Germany?
What type of visa or residence permit can you obtain for a long‑term stay?
Do you expect to become a German tax resident after moving?
How does your expected cost of living in Germany compare to your current location?
What is your current level of German language proficiency?

possibilities.text: Your taxable income might be subject to German tax rates.
possibilities.mechanism: German tax law taxes residents on worldwide income.
possibilities.downstream: Higher taxes could reduce net earnings.
possibilities.uncertainty: Check the tax treaty between Germany and your current country.

possibilities.text: You may retain non‑resident tax status in Germany.
possibilities.mechanism: Spending less than the residency threshold keeps you non‑resident for tax purposes.
possibilities.downstream: You continue paying tax only in your home country.
possibilities.uncertainty: Verify the number of days allowed for non‑resident status.

possibilities.text: Frequent travel could increase administrative overhead.
possibilities.mechanism: Multiple entries and exits require tracking and possible extensions.
possibilities.downstream: Time spent on paperwork may reduce free time.
possibilities.uncertainty: Assess the renewal process and costs for the permit.

missingEvidence: Exact visa category and eligibility criteria for remote workers.
Details of the tax treaty between Germany and your current country.
Projected monthly cost of living in the German city you are considering.
Your employer’s official remote‑work policy for overseas locations.
limitations: Assumes salary remains unchanged after the move.
Does not account for health‑insurance requirements in Germany.
Only high‑level cost‑of‑living differences are considered.
Language proficiency is treated as a categorical factor, not a skill gradient.

warnings: Left out 2 suggestions without a clear cause.
Left out speculative claims that failed checks.

path.name: Full relocation

known.answer: I expect the cost of living in Germany to be higher than in my current city.

Will you become a German tax resident

suggestions.text: Your taxable income might be subject to German tax rates.

body.change: The user told us: I expect the cost of living in Germany to be higher than in my current city..

suggestion.summary: Because your expectation that living costs will be higher in Germany could shrink your disposable income, the financial outcome of the relocation path may change.

add.trigger: cost of living turns out higher than in your current city
add.mechanism: Higher everyday expenses reduce the amount left after paying bills.
add.downstream: You may need to renegotiate your salary or cut discretionary spending.
add.uncertainty: If actual expenses are lower than expected, the impact on savings may be minimal.

add.text: You might need to adjust your budget for housing.
add.trigger: local rent prices are higher than anticipated
add.mechanism: Housing typically consumes a large share of monthly outlays.
add.downstream: A tighter budget could affect other lifestyle choices.
add.uncertainty: Finding a cheaper neighbourhood or shared accommodation could offset higher rents.

add.text: You could face a higher tax burden if you become a German tax resident.
add.mechanism: German tax rates apply to worldwide income for residents.
add.downstream: You may need to seek professional tax advice to optimise liabilities.
add.uncertainty: If you remain a non‑resident for tax purposes, the German tax impact would be limited.

add.text: You may need to improve German language skills for daily life.
add.mechanism: Limited language ability can make everyday tasks harder and increase reliance on services.
add.downstream: Investing time in language learning could ease integration and reduce hidden costs.
add.uncertainty: If you quickly reach intermediate proficiency, the impact lessens.

questions: How does the cost of housing, food, and transportation in your target German city compare to your current city?
Will you meet the criteria to become a German tax resident based on your stay duration and ties?
Does your employer’s remote‑work policy allow you to stay abroad for the long term without contract changes?
What level of German language proficiency is required for everyday activities like banking, healthcare, and shopping?
evidence: Cost‑of‑living indexes or local price surveys for the German city you plan to move to.
Official German tax residency guidelines and thresholds.
Your employer’s written remote‑work agreement or policy document.
